action: Scan the neck in transverse view. Identify the anatomy on the screen.
interpretation: Visualize two distinct tubular structures.

action: Observe the vessel characteristics to differentiate them.
interpretation: Identify the pulsatile ('versatile') structure as the carotid artery.

action: Focus on the adjacent vessel.
interpretation: Identify the non-pulsatile structure as the internal jugular vein.

action: Apply pressure over the vessels with the probe.
interpretation: Confirm anatomical identification through compression.

action: Observe the reaction of the vein to the pressure.
interpretation: Note that the jugular vein is totally compressible.

action: Release pressure or focus on the remaining patent vessel.
interpretation: Isolate the common carotid artery (CCA).

action: Rotate the probe 90 degrees from transverse to perpendicular.
interpretation: Transition to a long plane (sagittal) view of the carotid.

action: Optimize the B-mode image in longitudinal view.
interpretation: Visualize a healthy common carotid artery.

action: Measure the intima-media thickness (IMT).
interpretation: Ensure the thickness is less than 0.9 mm.

action: Reduce the TGC (Time Gain Compensation).
interpretation: Clear the image of noise or artifacts.

action: Activate Color Doppler mode.
interpretation: Apply the color box over the artery.

action: Adjust physics parameters: Increase depth and increase the velocity scale.
interpretation: Optimize the setting for arterial flow detection.

action: Reduce the color gain.
interpretation: Visualize the right common carotid artery with proper color filling and no bleeding artifacts.

action: Activate Pulse Wave (PW) Doppler.
interpretation: Prepare to take a spectral waveform.

action: Place the sample volume cursor exactly in the middle of the artery lumen.
interpretation: Target the area of maximum velocity (laminar flow center).

action: Freeze the image.
interpretation: Capture the spectral doppler trace.

action: Disable auto-calculation features.
interpretation: Prepare for manual measurement or clean visualization.

action: Inspect the spectral trace.
interpretation: Observe a nice waveform for the right CCA with a peak systolic velocity of 84.

action: Unfreeze and repeat the measurement. Move the sample volume to a different area of the artery.
interpretation: Sample multiple locations to ensure accuracy.

action: Measure the new velocity.
interpretation: Note the new velocity reading of 100.

action: Return to transverse view. Slide the probe cephalad (up), following the common carotid artery.
interpretation: Track the vessel superiorly.

action: Continue sliding superiorly until the vessel morphology changes.
interpretation: Reach the carotid bulb.

action: Trace the vessel carefully.
interpretation: Maintain visualization of the lumen.

action: Identify the segment where the diameter increases immediately before the bifurcation.
interpretation: Confirm position directly over the bulb.

action: Repeat the sweep from inferior (down) to superior (up).
interpretation: Verify findings.

action: Pause scanning where the diameter widens.
interpretation: Visualize the bulb.

action: Rotate the probe to the sagittal plane.
interpretation: Visualize the bulb in the longitudinal view.

action: Adjust TGC sliders.
interpretation: Optimize image quality/gain homogeneity.

action: Activate Color Doppler.
interpretation: Place the color box over the bulb.

action: Activate Pulse Wave Doppler at the bulb.
interpretation: Observe the initial waveform is 'bad' or suboptimal.

action: Steer ('stir') the doppler beam box.
interpretation: Adjust the angle to obtain good flow signal.

action: Document the velocity once flow signal improves.
interpretation: Observe better flow characteristics.

action: Freeze and measure.
interpretation: Record a velocity of 67.

action: Rotate the probe back to transverse view.
interpretation: Prepare to scan superiorly.

action: Scan superior to the bulb.
interpretation: Locate the bifurcation.

action: Identify the splitting of the vessels.
interpretation: Visualize the carotid bifurcating into the Internal Carotid Artery (ICA) and External Carotid Artery (ECA).

action: Apply Color Doppler.
interpretation: Use flow to confirm the presence of two distinct vessels.

action: Sweep through the bifurcation.
interpretation: Confirm the transition from one vessel into two distinct vessels (ICA and ECA).
